_meta.what: Which EPS measure Zacks reports per driver-model name (the measure our quarter calls are scored against) and the named items that convert the model's EPS basis to it. Read by valuation/eps_path.py (Kilian 2026-11-19 on the Self-scoring doc: 'this is not how you should do it; i suspect zacks is reporting adj. eps for some companies, you need to go find out what non-gaap measure they are using'). Replaces the median-of-gaps bridge.
_meta.items: forward conversion items, each computed from the engine's own forecast quarter (the model Sheet's lines): sbc = minus the quarter's stock comp x (1 - tax) / shares (tax 'quarter' = the quarter's own tax rate, or a number with its source); da = plus the quarter's D&A x (1 - tax) / shares. per_share basic_if_loss: a loss quarter goes on basic shares (diluted / basic ratio from the set's own share fields), as GAAP and Zacks report a loss.
_meta.zacks_source: Zacks reported EPS = data/earnings_miss.json / data/preprint_calendar.json history (Nasdaq.com earnings-surprise feed, Zacks data)
_meta.gaap_source: GAAP diluted EPS = SEC XBRL companyfacts us-gaap:EarningsPerShareDiluted (3-month periods; a fiscal Q4 is not tagged as a quarter)
_meta.model_gap: after the conversion, Zacks minus the engine's formula on a reported quarter (at that quarter's own filed tax) is a MODEL gap: an item the engine leaves out (interest income on net cash, other income, share-count timing). It is shown and flagged, never added: the model is fixed instead (rule 4/5, never carry a past quarter's gap forward).

items.why: 2026-11-25 (Kilian 'if any models cannot accurately model the business fix it'; audit/model_structure_1125.md): Zacks = company non-GAAP NI - SBC x (1 - tau), tau = the company's income tax effect of adjustments spread pro rata over its adjustments. That line = non-GAAP tax at 25% of non-GAAP pre-tax less the GAAP provision (Q2 FY27: 25% x 313.8 = 78.4 - 3.4 = 75.0 filed; Q1 FY27: 25% x 197.3 = 49.3 + 1.1 = 50.4 filed), so the SBC shield moves with profit and GAAP tax: Q2 FY27 456.4 / 502.1 x 75.0 = 68.2 (14.9%) -> Zacks (235.3 - 456.4 + 68.2) / 349.3 = -0.438 (-0.44 reported); Q1 FY27 433.7 / 494.0 x 50.4 = 44.3 (10.2%) -> (148.0 - 433.7 + 44.3) / 345.4 = -0.699 (-0.70 reported). The old fixed 14.7% fit Q2 only (Q1 off ~0.06).
items.gaap_tax_src: GAAP provision / revenue, FY2025 4.1 + FY2026 17.1 + H1 FY2027 2.3 = 23.5 on revenue 3,626.4 + 4,683.9 + 2,937.8 (XBRL IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit, Revenues; 10-K FY26, 10-Q Q2 FY27): 0.209% of revenue; H1 FY27 provision 2.3 on pre-tax loss (484.9): no tax benefit booked on US losses, so the provision is the foreign / state current tax that scales with the business; kept for forecast quarters with GAAP pre-tax above 0 from ~FY2029 (NOL carryforwards shelter it; a valuation-allowance release is a one-off, not forecast).
items.other_adj_src: Amortization of acquired intangibles from the 10-Q Q2 FY27 expected-amortization table (XBRL FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsAmortizationExpense*: remainder FY27 85.9, FY28 132.8, FY29 86.7, FY30 66.9; by quarter evenly) + amortization of debt issuance costs (Q2 FY27 2.081 on 2,300 of 2027/2029 notes, 2027 share x 888.2/1,150 after the repurchase, to maturities 2027-10-01 / 2029-10-01; new notes ~50 of costs = 3,750 principal - ~3,700 net proceeds (Ex.99.2), by principal over 2026-10-01 to 2029-10-15 / 2031-10-15). Restructuring, impairment and acquisition expenses: 0 (not forecastable). The Q3 FY27 2027-note repurchase premium (548.3 for 261.8, ~286) is left out of both, as the set assumes.
